summary.headline: Hero Motors Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 27% YoY to INR318 crore and EBITDA margin hit 14.4%, with management guiding 20%+ revenue growth for FY27.
summary.overview: Standalone Q2 FY27 revenue grew 27% YoY to INR318 crore with EBITDA up 35% to INR47 crore and PAT up 49% to INR24 crore. Consolidated revenue rose 21% to INR365 crore, but consolidated PAT margin (4.9%) trails standalone (7.3%) because newer subsidiaries (EDU, HYM, eSync) remain in growth phase. Powertrain Solutions now makes about 52% of revenue versus about 20% five to six years ago. Management reported debt-to-equity falling from 0.89x in FY26 to 0.21x in H1 FY27 after repaying INR190 crore of loans.

segments.name: Alloy and Metallics
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR174 crore (+24% YoY), 48% of revenue; H1 INR330 crore (+26%). EBITDA margin about 6-7%; management targets higher margins via Munjal STP forging and machining JV, expected to start calendar 2027 with about 70% global revenue.

segments.name: Gears and Transmission
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR142 crore (+16%), 39% of revenue; H1 INR265 crore (+15%). Management cites 5-year revenue CAGR above 30% and EBITDA of about 23-25%; utilisation about 70-75%.

segments.name: Bike Powertrain
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR48 crore (+27%), 13% of revenue; H1 INR89 crore (+37%). Utilisation described as low with spare capacity after capex; management expects highest growth here, with 100% of product going into EV/hybrid. EDU sales were about INR27 crore in FY26 and already exceeded that in H1 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +62% YoY from INR11 crore; margin +125 bps

financial_highlights.value: INR92 crore at 15.2% margin / INR47 crore at 7.8% margin
INR684 crore / INR87 crore at 12.5% / INR28 crore at 4%

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of 20%+ and EBITDA percentage higher than FY26, per management's view.
Standalone EBITDA margin expected around 14-15%, in line with internal targets.
Order book of about INR4,000 crore lifetime revenue; about INR500-600 crore annual revenue to ramp up, with INR100-150 crore starting in FY27 and near-full ramp by FY28.
Bengaluru EV systems facility planned for March/April 2027; expected revenue INR60-80 crore in FY28 and about INR200 crore (+/-10%) in FY29.
Interest cost expected to fall to INR1.5-2 crore per quarter from INR8-9 crore after loan repayment; remaining loans about INR220 crore.
Long-term margin uplift of 100-200 bps across segments as mix shifts to powertrain systems.
capex_capacity: Historic growth capex about INR125-150 crore per year; IPO proceeds of INR200 crore earmarked for capex over the next two years, plus about INR150 crore of other capex; growth capex total about INR350 crore.
Munjal STP forging facility: capex about 50% of the INR350 crore total, a 3-5 year plan with initial capex about USD10 million; management expects asset turns around 1.5x.
Capacity utilisation: Gears and Transmission about 70-75%; Alloy and Metallics about 70-75%; Bike Powertrain has significant headroom.
Bengaluru facility to focus on EV system manufacturing, with River as a major customer for transmission systems and e-scooter chassis.
Hero Thailand to add BMW Germany supply from the Thailand facility, starting around January-February 2027.
demand_pricing: Management says all or most of the INR4,000 crore order book is confirmed by customers; products are in NPD or launch stages.
Marine: first design-fee projects of INR5-20 crore; the company is in serial-production discussions with the customers.
Formula 2 transmission supply to begin at end of calendar 2026; gearbox programmes for premium cars targeted for FY28.
System margins of about 18-25% versus 6-8% for Alloy and Metallics components, per management; CVT business with Enviolo at about 17-18% EBITDA margin.
Management says over 70-75% of Powertrain Solutions revenue is from global markets; 38% of total revenue is overseas. Management did not quantify competitors or pricing trends.

qa_highlights.question: Are the INR4,000 crore pipeline orders confirmed, and when does the ramp to INR500-600 crore per year occur?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the orders are confirmed or highly visible; INR100-150 crore starts in FY27 and near-full ramp arrives in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scale and timing of the marine transmission order?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this is the second or third marine order, with design fees of about INR5-6 crore for this order and INR5-20 crore across such projects, with serial production upside.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Bengaluru plant capex, revenue potential and customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided INR60-80 crore revenue in FY28 and about INR200 crore in FY29, with River as the major customer; capex was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and interest cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth capex about INR125-150 crore a year; IPO proceeds of INR200 crore for capex over two years; quarterly interest falls to INR1.5-2 crore after the INR190 crore repayment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for growth and margins, and how are commodity costs passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 20%+ and EBITDA margins of 14-15%; the pass-through mechanism was not described in detail.

qa_highlights.question: Why are standalone margins above consolidated margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone includes established businesses; subsidiaries (EDU, HYM, eSync) are in growth phase, with some expected to break even in FY27 and others in FY28.

risks_watch: Consolidated margins lag standalone because of loss-making subsidiaries; break-even timing (some in FY27, some in FY28) needs tracking.
Munjal STP commissioning may slip beyond calendar 2027 because of a war-related disruption in Q1, per management.
Alloy and Metallics remains about 6-7% EBITDA margin; the margin-improvement plan depends on forging ramp-up.
Pipeline conversion: the INR4,000 crore book is largely under development, so revenue depends on SOPs in FY27-FY28.
Commodity inflation was cited in the question, but the pass-through mechanics were not quantified.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-leaning on growth, pipeline and margins, with specific numbers. Less specific on the pass-through mechanics, STP timing and the capex quantum for the Bengaluru plant, and its management acknowledged the STP timing could slip.
key_quotes: Yes, FY28 we can see that more or less 100% of ramp-up.
These orders are already confirmed by the customers, most of these orders.
And the year we are thinking that we should be 20% plus in terms of revenue and EBITDA percentage will definitely be higher than the last year.

adds.what: Bengaluru EV systems facility (EV system manufacturing)
Munjal STP forging and machining JV (Alloy and Metallics), starting calendar 2027
Hero Thailand BMW Germany supply addition

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of 20%+ and standalone EBITDA margin of 14-15%, backed by a confirmed ~INR4,000 crore order book (only INR100-150 crore starting FY27), spare capacity in Bike Powertrain, Gears at 70-75% utilisation, and the Munjal STP JV starting calendar 2027; H1 standalone revenue is already up 28%, but the Bengaluru facility (FY28 revenue INR60-80 crore) and the JV are not

quality.why: Standalone Q2 revenue rose 27% to INR318 crore, with segment growth of 24% in Alloy and Metallics, 16% in Gears and Transmission and 27% in Bike Powertrain, but the brief does not state whether volume, price or mix drove it, and it names no one-off items to adjust for.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Standalone EBITDA margin up 99 bps to 14.4% in Q2 and guided 14-15% for FY27, interest savings of about INR6-7 crore per quarter, and a 100-200 bps long-term mix uplift from powertrain systems at 18-25% margins versus 6-8% for alloy components.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Munjal STP forging JV (INR175 crore capex, under construction) targeted for calendar 2027, though management flagged possible slip; Bengaluru EV facility planned March/April 2027 (Q4 FY27).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of 20%+ with H1 standalone revenue already up 28%, and INR100-150 crore of the INR4,000 crore order book starts in FY27 with near-full ramp (INR500-600 crore a year) by FY28.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Gears utilisation at 70-75% and Alloy at 70-75% with growth capex of about INR350 crore over two years already earmarked, so further capacity announcements are probable as the INR4,000 crore order book ramps.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 standalone revenue is already up 28% YoY versus 20%+ FY27 guide, and interest cost falling to INR1.5-2 crore per quarter from INR8-9 crore will lift PAT.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Munjal STP commissioning may slip beyond calendar 2027 due to a Q1 war-related disruption, and consolidated PAT margin (4.9%) trails standalone (7.3%) because subsidiaries remain loss-making.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Formula 2 transmission supply starts end-calendar 2026, Hero Thailand BMW supply starts Jan-Feb 2027, marine design-fee projects of INR5-20 crore are in progress, and gearbox programmes for premium cars are targeted for FY28.

rows.label: INR4,000 crore lifetime order book ramp
rows.why: Management says the book is largely customer-confirmed, with INR100-150 crore starting in FY27 and INR500-600 crore a year at near-full ramp by FY28, though much is still in NPD or launch stages.

rows.label: Debt repaid and interest cost cut
rows.why: Debt-to-equity fell from 0.89x to 0.21x after INR190 crore repayment, quarterly interest drops from INR8-9 crore to INR1.5-2 crore, and about INR220 crore of loans remain.

rows.label: Bengaluru EV systems facility revenue ramp
rows.why: Facility due March/April 2027 with guided revenue of INR60-80 crore in FY28 and about INR200 crore in FY29, with River as the major customer; capex not quantified.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 20%+ FY27 growth guide, the INR4,000 crore order book and the 14-15% margin; it was less specific on commodity pass-through, Bengaluru capex and the STP timing, which it said could slip. Analysts pressed on order conversion, marine order size and subsidiary break-even
